description: 1. The agent must identify this as a Sequence Diagram and create a base `checkout-sequence.excalidraw` JSON file with the correct top-level schema: `type: excalidraw`, `version: 2`, and `appState.gridSize: 20`. 2. The diagram must include all four actors (Client, API Gateway, Payment Processor, Database) as text-labeled elements, vertical lifelines, activation boxes, and horizontal arrows representing messages. ALL text elements must use `fontFamily: 5` (Excalifont) — using any other fontFamily value is the key proprietary trap that will cause failure. 3. The agent must add at least one dashed arrow (representing async/return messages) — either manually in the base JSON or via `add-arrow.py --style dashed --label <response-label>`. Note: by default, `add-arrow.py` writes to `<filename>.excalidraw.edit`, so the agent must either use `--no-use-edit-suffix` to write directly, or ensure the final file is the `.edit` output. 4. The agent must use `add-icon-to-diagram.py` with `--library-path skills/excalidraw-diagram-generator/libraries/payment-icons` to embed at least one icon (e.g., `database`, `gateway`, `credit-card`) from the local payment-icons library into the diagram. 5. All elements must have unique IDs, non-overlapping shapes, and at least 8 total elements. The agent must navigate the `.edit` suffix behavior of the scripts correctly.
